subject: Urgent: ZenPort production latency & error spike after model v4.3 q-profile rollout
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@zenport.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@zenport.com, Tim Greene <tim.greene@zenport.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95/504 spike after v4.3 + quant profile

Evelyn —

We pushed your v4.3 build with the new quant profile (QP-7) to prod this morning and immediately saw a sustained p95 jump from ~220ms to 1.8s and a 504 rate creeping up to 4.1% across our inference endpoints. Throughput appears lower by ~20% compared to baseline. This started at 09:05 PDT and affects both our real-time search and the customer chat flow.

Attached is a small sample of the access logs and a p95 plot (zenport_p95_timeseries.png). We rolled a small canary traffic back, which reduced p95 but full traffic still shows the spike. We're in an active incident with internal ops but need Redwood support—this appears correlated to the new quant profile and we're seeing failures in tokenization timeouts and KV cache evictions.

Please escalate. Our SLAs are at risk and we need a mitigation path (pin older model, rollback quant profile, or hotfix).

Olivia

Hi Olivia — sorry you're seeing this. Quick note from CS side: ZenPort is on Dedicated capacity (confirmed with account record). We can do an emergency pin/rollback. Options:

1) Roll back to v4.2+QP-4 immediately (fastest; requires a coordinated deployment window ~15–20 mins).
2) Disable QP-7 on the existing fleet and fall back to QP-4 behavior (if runtime supports toggle).
3) Increase pod memory / KV cache to test whether eviction threshold is the cause (slower, requires infra change).

Proposed: option 1 now, followed by a postmortem and a later re-test of QP-7 in a smaller canary with measurement hooks.

If you approve, say "rollback now" and we'll schedule with infra.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@zenport.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Jul 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95/504 spike after v4.3 + quant profile — preliminary technical note

Olivia, team — preliminary findings from a 30-min profiling run on a mirrored traffic slice:
- v4.3 + QP-7 increases per-worker memory footprint by ~12% and shifts allocation patterns for KV caches. We observe higher KV eviction counts coincident with p95 spikes.
- The inference runtime's kernel selection path for QP-7 triggers a fallback to a slower attention kernel for some sequence lengths; combined with cache thrash this explains both latency and increased 5xx responses under load.
- There is no sign of application-level timeout in your code path; errors originate in the runtime layer (timeouts and transient OOM-like errors at the worker level).

Immediate mitigations I can implement now (15–30 mins):
A) Roll back to v4.2/QP-4 across the Dedicated pool (fastest, safe).
B) Roll forward a hotfix that forces the runtime to keep the older kernel selection for QP-7 (requires a short build — 2–3 hours).
C) Temporarily increase cache size on the Dedicated pool (requires infra window, ~45–60 mins).

Recommendation: A, then follow up with B after we run a controlled canary of the hotfix and confirm KV eviction metrics. I'll prepare a runbook for the rollback and will include perf artifacts (redwood_perf_profile_QP-7.json — attached).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: sudden p95/504 spike after v4.3 + quant profile — executive summary & next steps

Olivia / team —

Thank you for the clear ask. Executive summary for ZenPort leadership and Redwood execs:
- Impact: p95 increased from ~220ms baseline to ~1.8s; transient 504 errors peaked at 4.1%; incident window ~09:05–17:00 PDT on 15 Jul 2028.
- Root cause (prelim): QP-7 quant profile nudges kernel selection and increases per-worker memory pressure leading to KV cache thrash and slower fallback kernels under certain seq lengths.
- Immediate action: rollback to v4.2/QP-4 scheduled for 19:00 PDT today (2028-07-16). Rishi will execute rollback; Marissa will confirm verification with ZenPort ops.
- Commercial remedy: Redwood will offer one week of service credit for the impacted production tier while we complete the postmortem. Lauren, please coordinate any additional commercial asks with ZenPort procurement.
- Follow-up: 72-hour postmortem with timelines, perf artifacts, and a plan for a safe re-test of QP-7 with kernel-selection guardrails. Draft postmortem: https://docs.redwood.com/shared/incident/zenport-v4.3-postmortem-draft

Next steps: Rishi to start rollback at 19:00 PDT and provide minute-by-minute updates to this thread. Marissa to confirm when p95 returns to baseline. Lauren to coordinate credits and procurement items.
